newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK short cash rates up on quarter-end demand.
newsitem.headline: HK short cash rates up on quarter-end demand.

text.p: Hong Kong short cash rates were up Monday on quarter-end demand, dealers said.
Interbank overnight rates stood at 5-5/8 9/16 percent at Monday midday, up from Friday's 5-3/16 1/16. Three-month traded at 5-9/16 1/2 percent, hardly changed from 5-9/16 7/16.
"At the end of a quarter, banks often square their positions and keep cash," a local bank dealer said.
The government paper market was quiet, dealers said.
One-week Exchange Fund bills yielded 5.05 percent versus 5.11, while three-year notes yielded 6.50 percent versus 6.52.
Yields of five-year notes stood unchanged at 7.18 percent. Seven-year note yields dipped to 7.51 percent from 7.53.
